rows: Card brand (visa/mastercard/amex/discover/diners/jcb) by prefix+length, or NULL

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
## `card_brand(text)`

Returns `VARCHAR`: the card **brand** -- one of `visa`, `mastercard`, `amex`, `discover`, `diners`, `jcb` -- inferred from the IIN/BIN prefix and length, or `NULL` when the number matches no known brand or is `NULL`. Separators are ignored.

Classification is by prefix+length only and does **not** require a passing Luhn checksum (so malformed PANs can still be tagged); use `is_valid_card` for the checksum. See `card_brands()` for the full brand list.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
# `card_brand`

Identify a card's brand from its prefix and length.

## Usage

```sql
SELECT conform.card_brand('4111111111111111');  -- 'visa'
```

## Notes

- Prefix+length only; independent of the Luhn check.
- `card_brands()` lists every brand this can return.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Detect the card brand", "sql": "SELECT conform.main.card_brand('4111111111111111')"}]
rows.vgi.title: Detect Card Brand

rows: The brands card_brand() can return (visa, mastercard, amex, ...)

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
## `card_brands()`

A **table function** (no arguments) returning one row per card brand the `card_brand` scalar can emit, with a single column:

- `brand` (`VARCHAR`) -- a brand name such as `visa`, `mastercard`, `amex`, `discover`, `diners`, `jcb`.

Use it to enumerate the recognized brands -- e.g. to populate a UI filter or to validate that a `card_brand(...)` result is within the known set.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
# `card_brands`

Discovery table of every brand `card_brand()` can return.

## Columns

- `brand` (`VARCHAR`) -- e.g. `visa`, `mastercard`, `amex`.

Returns `VARCHAR`: the two-letter ISO country code that prefixes a valid IBAN (e.g. `'GB'`), or `NULL` when the IBAN is invalid or `NULL`.

True if the card number's digits pass the Luhn checksum

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
## `is_valid_card(text)`

Returns `BOOLEAN`: `true` when the card number's digits pass the **Luhn** checksum, `false` otherwise, `NULL` when `text` is `NULL`. Separators (spaces, dashes) are ignored.

Luhn catches typos and many fabricated numbers but does **not** prove a card exists or is active. Note that validity is independent of brand: use `card_brand` to classify (a number can have a recognized brand yet fail Luhn, and vice versa).
rows.vgi.doc_md:
# `is_valid_card`

Check a card number against the Luhn checksum.

## Usage

```sql
SELECT conform.is_valid_card('4111 1111 1111 1111');  -- true
```

## Notes

- Luhn only -- not an authorization or existence check.
- Independent of `card_brand`.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Validate a card number via Luhn", "sql": "SELECT conform.main.is_valid_card('4111 1111 1111 1111')"}]

rows: True if text is a syntactically valid email address (no DNS lookup)

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
## `is_valid_email(text)`

Returns `BOOLEAN`: `true` when `text` is a **syntactically** valid email address, `false` when it is not, and `NULL` when `text` is `NULL`.

Validation is **offline** -- it checks address syntax and normalizes the domain, but performs **no DNS or deliverability lookup**, so it is fast, deterministic, and never makes a network call.

Use it to gate or filter a column of user-supplied email values (`WHERE conform.is_valid_email(email)`), or as a quality check before loading contact data. Pair with `normalize_email` to canonicalize the values you keep.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
# `is_valid_email`

Test whether a string is a syntactically valid email address.

## Usage

```sql
SELECT conform.is_valid_email('a@b.com');   -- true
SELECT conform.is_valid_email('not-email');  -- false
```

## Notes

- Offline only -- no DNS / deliverability check.
- `NULL` in yields `NULL` out; any non-`NULL` invalid value yields `false`.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Valid email", "sql": "SELECT conform.main.is_valid_email('a@b.com')"}]
rows.vgi.title: Is Valid Email Address

Returns `BOOLEAN`: `true` when `text` is a structurally valid International Bank Account Number -- correct per-country length and a passing **mod-97 checksum** -- `false` otherwise, `NULL` when `text` is `NULL`. Spaces are tolerated.

Backed by `python-stdnum`; offline and deterministic. Use it to validate bank account fields before payment processing. Pair with `format_iban` for display and `iban_country` to extract the country.

rows: True if text matches a country's postal-code format (modest coverage: US, CA, GB, DE, FR, NL, AU, JP, IN, BR). Unknown country raises an error.

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
## `is_valid_postal_code(text, country)`

Returns `BOOLEAN`: `true` when `text` matches the postal-code **format** for `country` (ISO-3166 alpha-2), `false` when it does not, `NULL` when `text` is `NULL`.

Coverage is intentionally modest -- a per-country regex table for US, CA, GB, DE, FR, NL, AU, JP, IN, BR. This is a **format** check, not deliverability validation. An **unknown** `country` raises an error (rather than silently returning `false`) so a country typo is not mistaken for an invalid code. `country` is a required constant.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
# `is_valid_postal_code`

Format-check a postal code for a country.

## Usage

```sql
SELECT conform.is_valid_postal_code('90210', 'US');     -- true
SELECT conform.is_valid_postal_code('K1A 0B1', 'CA');   -- true
```

## Notes

- Supported: US, CA, GB, DE, FR, NL, AU, JP, IN, BR.
- Unknown `country` raises an error (caught typos, not silent `false`).

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
## `mask_card(text)`

Returns `VARCHAR`: the card number with every digit except the **last four** replaced by `*` (e.g. `'************1111'`), or `NULL` when the input has fewer than four digits or is `NULL`.

Use it to safely display or log PANs without exposing the full number (PCI-friendly redaction). Separators are stripped before masking, so the output is a contiguous masked string.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
# `mask_card`

Redact a card number, keeping only the last four digits.

## Usage

```sql
SELECT conform.mask_card('4111-1111-1111-1111');  -- '************1111'
```

## Notes

- Keeps the last 4 digits; `NULL` if fewer than 4 digits.
- Separators are stripped before masking.

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
## `normalize_email(text)`

Returns `VARCHAR`: a **canonical** form of the email address (the domain lower-cased and IDNA-normalized; the local-part case left intact per the email standard), or `NULL` when `text` is invalid or `NULL`.

Validation is offline (no DNS). Use this before grouping, joining, or deduplicating on email so that `Test@Example.COM` and `Test@example.com` collapse to the same key (differently-cased local parts stay distinct). Combine with `is_valid_email` if you also need a validity flag.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
# `normalize_email`

Canonicalize an email address for comparison / deduplication.

## Usage

```sql
SELECT conform.normalize_email('Test@Example.COM');  -- 'Test@example.com'
```

## Notes

- Lower-cases the domain; leaves the local-part case unchanged.
- Returns `NULL` for invalid or `NULL` input.

Lower-case scheme + host and strip a default port, or NULL if invalid

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
## `normalize_url(text)`

Returns `VARCHAR`: a canonicalized URL -- scheme and host lower-cased and a default port (`:80` for http, `:443` for https) stripped -- or `NULL` when the URL is invalid or `NULL`.

Normalize before comparing, grouping, or deduplicating URLs so trivial variants (`HTTP://Example.com:80/Path` vs `http://example.com/Path`) collapse. Path/query case is preserved. Offline.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
# `normalize_url`

Canonicalize a URL for comparison / deduplication.

## Usage

```sql
SELECT conform.normalize_url('HTTP://Example.com:80/Path');
-- 'http://example.com/Path'
```

## Notes

- Lower-cases scheme+host, strips default port; keeps path/query case.

## `phone_region(text, region)`

Returns `VARCHAR`: the ISO-3166 alpha-2 region a phone number belongs to, parsing `text` with the explicit `region` (so national-format numbers resolve correctly), or `NULL` when invalid or `NULL`.

Use this overload when input is in national format for a known non-US country. `region` is a constant.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
# `phone_region` (with region)

Determine a number's region, parsing in an explicit region.

## Usage

```sql
SELECT conform.phone_region('07400 123456', 'GB');  -- 'GB'
```

## Notes

- `region` is an ISO-3166 alpha-2 constant used for parsing.

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
## `supported_phone_regions()`

A **table function** (no arguments) returning one row per phone region the phone scalars understand, with columns:

- `region` (`VARCHAR`) -- the ISO-3166 alpha-2 code you pass as the optional `region` argument to `is_valid_phone(text, region)`, the phone formatters, `phone_region`, and `phone_type`.
- `country_code` (`INTEGER`) -- its international dialling (country calling) code.

Use it to discover valid region values or to look up a country's dialling code (filter by `region` to read one country's `country_code`).

The countries is_valid_postal_code() understands (US, CA, GB, DE, ...)

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
## `supported_postal_countries()`

A **table function** (no arguments) returning one row per country whose postal-code format `is_valid_postal_code(text, country)` can check, with a single column:

- `country` (`VARCHAR`) -- an ISO-3166 alpha-2 code such as `US`, `CA`, `GB`, `DE`, `FR`, `NL`, `AU`, `JP`, `IN`, `BR`.

Coverage is intentionally modest. Because `is_valid_postal_code` **raises** on an unsupported country (so a typo is not mistaken for an invalid code), read this table first -- or join against it -- to confirm a country is supported before calling the scalar.

Lower-cased host of a valid URL, or NULL if invalid

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
## `url_host(text)`

Returns `VARCHAR`: the lower-cased **host** (domain) of a valid URL (e.g. `'www.example.com'`), or `NULL` when the URL is invalid or `NULL`.

Use it to group or filter by site/domain, build allow/deny lists, or join URL data on host. The port and userinfo are excluded; only the host is returned. Offline.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
# `url_host`

Extract the (lower-cased) host from a URL.

## Usage

```sql
SELECT conform.url_host('https://WWW.Example.com/a');  -- 'www.example.com'
```

## Notes

- Host only (no port/userinfo); `NULL` for invalid URLs.
